result.note: Tests the February 2026 India-Greece Joint Declaration of Intent (venue, linked reform agendas, cooperation plans) and the five-year industrial cooperation plan.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, India and Greece signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on defence cooperation. Consider the following statements:
items: It was signed at a meeting of the two defence ministers held in Athens.
It aligns India's Aatmanirbhar Bharat goals with Greece's Agenda 2030 military reforms.
It was accompanied by a 2026 Military Cooperation Plan for joint exercises.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The first statement is wrong because Rajnath Singh and Nikolaos-Georgios Dendias met in New Delhi, not Athens. The other two are correct. The declaration aims at joint production of advanced military technology.
questions.source: Both nations signed a Joint Declaration of Intent to partner India’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliance) goals with Greece’s Agenda 2030 military reforms.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, India and Greece set in motion a plan for defence industrial cooperation. What is the duration of this plan?
questions.explain: The defence ministers' meeting in New Delhi put a five-year plan for industrial cooperation in play. TBB reads the deepening ties with Greece, Turkey's main rival, as a counter-alignment as Turkey eyes a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
questions.source: A five-year plan for industrial cooperation is now in play, alongside a 2026 Military Cooperation Plan for joint exercises.
